newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. wheat rejected by China offered to Manila.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wheat rejected by China offered to Manila.

text.p: American commodity traders had offered to sell at a discount 70,000 tonnes of U.S. winter wheat rejected by China to Philippine noodle manufacturers, local flour executives and traders said on Wednesday.
"They (traders) said the wheat was loaded in two ships moored in a China port," an executive in a local flour mill said.

American commodity traders had offered the wheat at a discount to Philippine buyers after the shipments were rejected by China allegedly because the wheat was tainted with fungus, Manila traders said.

An official of the U.S. Agricultural Trade Office said early this month in Shanghai that about 150,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat tainted by a fungus known as TCK smut is sitting in ships off the Chinese ports of Shanghai and Fuzhou.
